titulo: Shopping, clothes, colors and demonstratives: Clothes and the first colors

aula.objetivo: Name clothes and colors, point at things with «este, esse, aquele», ask the price, say your size and buy something in a shop.

blocos.titulo: Clothes and colors: the color comes after the noun and agrees with it
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: every piece of clothing has a gender you must know: «a camiseta, a camisa, a calça, o vestido, o sapato, o tênis, o casaco». A pair of trousers is usually «uma calça» (singular) in Brazilian speech; «as calças» in the plural is also correct. «Tênis» does not change in the plural: «um tênis, dois tênis». STEP 2: colors are adjectives and come after the noun: «uma camisa branca», «um casaco preto». The English order (white shirt) is wrong in Portuguese. STEP 3: colors ending in -o change like any adjective: «branco, branca, brancos, brancas»; «preto, preta, pretos, pretas»; «vermelho, vermelha, vermelhos, vermelhas». STEP 4: colors ending in -e or -l have one form for masculine and feminine: «verde, verdes»; «azul» becomes «azuis» in the plural (the -l changes to -is). STEP 5: to say what you wear, use «usar»: «Eu uso camiseta branca no trabalho». It is a regular -ar verb: uso, usa, usamos, usam.
blocos.comparacao: In English the color comes before the noun (a white shirt) and never changes (white shirts). In Portuguese it follows the noun and agrees in gender and number: «uma camisa branca», «duas camisas brancas». Also note «usar» means both «to wear» and «to use»: «Eu uso tênis» (I wear sneakers) and «Eu uso o celular» (I use the cell phone).

exemplos.pt: The blue T-shirts are over there.

exemplos.ru: Ele usa calça preta e tênis branco.
exemplos.pt: He wears black trousers and white sneakers.

erros.motivo: The color agrees with the noun, and «camisa» is feminine.
In Portuguese the color comes after the noun.
Words ending in -l change to -is in the plural: azul, azuis.

blocos.enunciado: Say what you are wearing now, with the color: «Eu uso uma camiseta azul e calça preta.» Then describe what a friend or a family member usually wears.
Say the numbers from 20 to 100 in tens aloud (vinte, trinta, quarenta…), then say three prices in reais as you would in a café: «Custa dez reais», «São quarenta e cinco reais».
